notes: Decision order: first the OTP check (otpPattern) on the whole body, then the sender match (a bank applies when its senderPattern is a substring of the sender; no bank means unknown_template), then the first template whose regex matches wins.
A template of kind ignore returns its ignoreReason. A body from a known sender that matches no template is unknown_template if it matches both moneyVerbPattern and amountPattern, otherwise not_money.

moneyVerbPattern and amountPattern are deliberately broad (a false keep beats a lost transaction): verbs debited, credited, spent, deducted, paid, received, withdrawn, sent, transferred, refunded, reversed and 'payment of'; an amount is INR, USD, Rs, Rs. or the rupee sign (U+20B9, written as a \u20B9 JSON escape) before or after a digit. Bare 'payment', 'credit' and 'debit' are left out because statements and card names use them (fixture idfc-052). Card payment thank-you messages are kept out by the card_payment_thanks ignore template, which is checked first.

All patterns are case-insensitive and use only syntax valid in both JavaScript and Java. Any extraction fault in a matched template (bad month, day outside 1-31, month outside 1-12, no digits in the amount) yields unknown_template, never an exception.
When the body has no date, occurredOn is the Asia/Kolkata date of receivedAt (UTC+05:30, so the day boundary is 18:30 UTC) and occurredTime is null.
Times with AM/PM convert to 24-hour: 12:xx AM becomes 00:xx, 12:xx PM stays 12:xx, other PM hours add 12.

Before the OTP check and matching, both engines replace every character in U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+FEFF, U+2028 and U+2029 with a plain space (Java's \s is ASCII-only, JS's is not).
Currency Rs or Rs. means INR. Group names allowed: amount, currency, day, month, year, time, last4, counterparty, utr, merchant, balance.
